title: Insider Trading and Securities Dealing Policy

tiers.name: All Persons
tiers.description: All directors, officers, and employees of AVITA Medical, as well as certain consultants, contractors, or other individuals retained by AVITA Medical. Subject to the MNPI trading/tipping prohibition, the short sale and hedging prohibitions, the margin/pledging pre-clearance requirement, and the open-window trading restriction.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: Directors, officers, executive leadership team members, certain employees who work in accounting, finance, legal, compliance, investor relations, commercial operations, and sales, as well as any other person who may have increased access to material non-public information. Must pre-clear any intended transaction with the General Counsel at least two trading days in advance, and may not sell or purchase AVITA Medical securities of the same class within six months of an open-market purchase or sale.

tiers.name: Section 16 Individuals
tiers.description: Directors, executive officers, or other reporting persons under Section 16 of the Exchange Act. Subject to Section 16 short-swing profit disgorgement rules and same-day reporting to the General Counsel and CFO.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: Family members or anyone residing in your household, family members not residing in your household whose transactions you direct or influence, and any corporation, partnership or trust that you or a related person influences or controls. Transactions by Restricted Persons are treated as if undertaken by, or for the benefit of, the covered person.

definitions.hedging_definition: financial instruments (e.g., swaps, collars, forward contracts, etc.) that are designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of AVITA Medical securities, including both vested and unvested securities

windows.start_anchor: fourteen days before the last day of AVITA Medical's fiscal quarter
windows.end_anchor: two Nasdaq trading days after the release of AVITA Medical's annual or quarterly earnings

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: AVITA Medical has the right to modify an open window period at any time and for any reason, or may decide that a trading window should not be opened at all during any quarter, effectively extending the closed period at the Company's discretion; not stated to be confidential. The Board, in its sole discretion, may separately approve additional open window periods.

rules.detail: Derivatives (such as put or call options) are expressly covered transactions. Non-Designated Persons need no pre-clearance but may only trade within designated open window periods and never while in possession of material non-public information.
rules.evidence: Transactions covered by this Policy include purchases and sales of shares of common stock, CDIs, any derivatives securities (such as put or call options) and any debt or other equity securities issued in the future by AVITA Medical or a Related Entity.

rules.section: PRE-CLEARANCE OF DEALINGS BY DESIGNATED PERSONS
rules.detail: Designated Persons must pre-clear any intended transaction, including derivatives, with the General Counsel at least two trading days in advance, and may only complete it within the open window period following approval.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons and their Restricted Persons must pre-clear any intended transaction in AVITA Medical securities with the General Counsel, including any transaction during any open window period, not less than two trading days before the date of the intended transaction.

rules.section: PROHIBITION ON SHORT SELLING, HEDGING TRANSACTIONS AND SHORT-TERM TRADING
rules.detail: Absolute, unqualified ban on hedging instruments -- collars are named expressly -- applying to every person covered by the Policy and to both vested and unvested securities, with no clearance override or exception stated anywhere in the Policy.
rules.evidence: you are prohibited from purchasing or using, directly or indirectly, financial instruments (e.g., swaps, collars, forward contracts, etc.) that are designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of AVITA Medical securities, including both vested and unvested securities.

rules.section: PROHIBITION ON SHORT SELLING, HEDGING TRANSACTIONS AND SHORT-TERM TRADING
rules.detail: Forward contracts (a common monetisation structure) are expressly named among the prohibited hedging instruments when designed to hedge or offset a decrease in the market value of the securities.
rules.evidence: financial instruments (e.g., swaps, collars, forward contracts, etc.) that are designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of AVITA Medical securities, including both vested and unvested securities.

rules.section: PROHIBITION ON SHORT SELLING, HEDGING TRANSACTIONS AND SHORT-TERM TRADING
rules.detail: Absolute ban, no clearance route stated.
rules.evidence: Consequently, short sales of AVITA Medical securities are prohibited.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy.

CFDs are not named specifically, but as a derivative security in respect of AVITA Medical securities they fall within covered transactions; if designed to hedge or offset a price decrease they would instead be prohibited outright under the hedging ban.
rules.evidence: Transactions covered by this Policy include purchases and sales of shares of common stock, CDIs, any derivatives securities (such as put or call options) and any debt or other equity securities issued in the future by AVITA Medical or a Related Entity.

rules.section: PRE-CLEARANCE ON USE OF MARGIN ACCOUNTS AND PLEDGING OF SECURITIES
rules.detail: Margin trading arrangements are expressly named and require General Counsel pre-clearance before entry; applies to every person covered by the Policy, not only Designated Persons.
rules.evidence: to the extent you desire to enter into a margin trading or pledging arrangement involving AVITA Medical securities, you must first obtain pre-clearance from the General Counsel.

rules.section: PRE-CLEARANCE ON USE OF MARGIN ACCOUNTS AND PLEDGING OF SECURITIES
rules.detail: Pledging AVITA Medical securities as collateral is expressly named and requires prior General Counsel pre-clearance.
rules.evidence: If your AVITA Medical securities are held in a margin account or pledged as collateral, they may be sold without your consent under certain circumstances. ... you must first obtain pre-clearance from the General Counsel.

rules.section: PRE-CLEARANCE ON USE OF MARGIN ACCOUNTS AND PLEDGING OF SECURITIES
rules.detail: Any margin trading or pledging arrangement involving the securities requires General Counsel pre-clearance before entry; no outright ban, but the underlying hedging ban would independently prohibit a collar structured alongside the loan.
rules.evidence: to the extent you desire to enter into a margin trading or pledging arrangement involving AVITA Medical securities, you must first obtain pre-clearance from the General Counsel.

rules.section: PROHIBITION ON SHORT SELLING, HEDGING TRANSACTIONS AND SHORT-TERM TRADING
rules.detail: Designated Persons who buy or sell in the open market may not sell or buy the same class of securities again for six months, with no stated exception route.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons (as defined herein) who purchase or sell AVITA Medical securities in the open market may not sell or purchase any AVITA Medical securities of the same class during the six months following the transaction.

rules.section: ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS ON CERTAIN DESIGNATED PERSONS
rules.detail: Not a policy prohibition but a statutory consequence: a matching purchase and sale (or sale and purchase) within six months requires disgorgement of all profits to AVITA Medical regardless of knowledge of material non-public information; some equity-plan award transactions may be exempt.
rules.evidence: Section 16 Individuals who make "matching" transactions of AVITA Medical's securities within a six-month period (e.g., a purchase within six months prior to a sale, or a sale within six months prior to a purchase) must disgorge all profits from such transactions to AVITA Medical whether or not they had knowledge of any material non-public information.

rules.detail: The six-month same-class restriction is expressly limited to Designated Persons; the Policy does not address short-term dealing by other employees beyond the open-window and MNPI rules.

clearance.post_trade_deadline: unspecified ('Subsequent confirmation of the transaction must be provided')
clearance.section: PRE-CLEARANCE OF DEALINGS BY DESIGNATED PERSONS
clearance.evidence: Designated Persons can only conduct transactions if: (i) the General Counsel approves the specified transaction; and (ii) such person is not otherwise in possession of material non-public information. ... if clearance is denied, the denial must be kept confidential and must not be disclosed to anyone.

clearance.section: PRE-CLEARANCE ON USE OF MARGIN ACCOUNTS AND PLEDGING OF SECURITIES
clearance.evidence: to the extent you desire to enter into a margin trading or pledging arrangement involving AVITA Medical securities, you must first obtain pre-clearance from the General Counsel.

clearance.approver: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer
clearance.post_trade_to: General Counsel and Chief Financial Officer
clearance.post_trade_deadline: same day (SEC filing required by the second business day after the transaction)
clearance.section: ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS ON CERTAIN DESIGNATED PERSONS
clearance.evidence: If you are a Section 16 Individual, you must immediately report to the General Counsel and the Chief Financial Officer all transactions ... AVITA Medical requires same day reporting due to SEC requirements that certain insider reports be filed with the SEC by the second business day after the date on which a reportable transaction occurs.

short_term.basis: from the open-market transaction; same class
short_term.evidence: Designated Persons (as defined herein) who purchase or sell AVITA Medical securities in the open market may not sell or purchase any AVITA Medical securities of the same class during the six months following the transaction.

short_term.basis: statutory short-swing profit rule under Exchange Act Section 16(b): matching purchase within 6 months of a sale, or sale within 6 months of a purchase
carve_outs: certain transactions, e.g. receipt of awards under AVITA Medical's equity incentive plan, may be exempted from Section 16(b)
short_term.evidence: Section 16 Individuals who make "matching" transactions of AVITA Medical's securities within a six-month period ... must disgorge all profits from such transactions to AVITA Medical.

exceptions.evidence: Certain transactions (e.g., receipt of awards under AVITA Medical's equity incentive plan) may be exempted from Section 16(b).

external_documents: AVITA Medical equity incentive plan (referenced for Section 16(b) exemption)
exemption_authority: None for individuals. There are no exceptions to the prohibition on trading while in possession of material non-public information ('Small transactions and transactions that may be necessary or justifiable for an independent reason ... are not excepted'), and no hardship, court order or other individual waiver mechanism is described for the open-window trading restriction, the hedging ban, or the short sale ban. The Board, in its sole discretion, may approve additional open window periods, and AVITA Medical may modify or decide not to open a window at all -- a Company-level scheduling power, not an individual exemption. The General Counsel's determinations and interpretations of the Policy are final and not subject to further review.

bespoke_clauses.clause: you are prohibited from purchasing or using, directly or indirectly, financial instruments (e.g., swaps, collars, forward contracts, etc.) that are designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of AVITA Medical securities, including both vested and unvested securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The exact product the bank wants to offer -- a collar -- is named and banned outright for every person covered by the Policy and for both vested and unvested holdings, with no clearance route, waiver, or exception anywhere in the document.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no exceptions to MNPI trading ban
bespoke_clauses.clause: There are no exceptions to this general prohibition. Small transactions and transactions that may be necessary or justifiable for an independent reason (e.g., raising money for a charity or an emergency) are not excepted.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the hedging ban were somehow structured around, there is no hardship or emergency-funding exception available to justify entering a collar or loan while holding material non-public information.

bespoke_clauses.clause: For the avoidance of doubt, no person covered by this Policy is permitted to trade or otherwise conduct transactions in AVITA Medical securities outside of the designated open window periods.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even setting the hedging ban aside, entry, adjustment or unwind of any structure would need to occur inside one of the quarterly open windows, and AVITA Medical can unilaterally shorten, modify or cancel a window at any time for any reason.

bespoke_clauses.topic: forced sale risk while holding MNPI
bespoke_clauses.clause: If your AVITA Medical securities are held in a margin account or pledged as collateral, they may be sold without your consent under certain circumstances. As a result, a margin or foreclosure sale of AVITA Medical securities could occur when you are otherwise in possession of material non-public information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The Policy itself flags that a lender's enforcement sale on the pledged shares could occur at a moment when the executive holds material non-public information or is otherwise outside an open window, which is precisely why pre-clearance is required before entering the arrangement at all.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The General Counsel is responsible for administering this Policy and all determinations and interpretations of this Policy by the General Counsel are final and not subject to further review.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no appeal from a General Counsel refusal of pre-clearance for the margin/pledging leg, and separately no override exists for the hedging ban regardless of General Counsel's view.

summary: A funded collar is prohibited outright under this policy. It expressly and unconditionally bans 'financial instruments (e.g., swaps, collars, forward contracts, etc.) that are designed to hedge or offset any decrease in the market value of AVITA Medical securities, including both vested and unvested securities' -- naming the exact structure -- for every director, officer, employee, consultant and their Restricted Persons, with no clearance route, waiver or exception stated anywhere in the Policy. Even apart from the hedging ban, short sales are separately prohibited outright, and the loan leg (a margin trading or pledging arrangement) independently requires prior General Counsel pre-clearance and, like any transaction, can only occur within the quarterly open window periods and never while in possession of material non-public information, a restriction the Policy says has no exceptions. Directors and executive officers who are Section 16 Individuals face the further statutory risk that settlement of any structure could be matched against another transaction within six months and trigger disgorgement of short-swing profits. Because the hedging ban is absolute and independently fatal, the funded collar cannot be implemented under this policy regardless of clearance, vesting status, or trading window.
